title: Office application starts a command or script interpreter
description: Detects a Microsoft Office application starting a selected command, script, or signed-binary interpreter in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process telemetry.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use an Office document or message to start an interpreter and execute code.
hypothesis.rationale: Office-to-interpreter process chains are useful execution signals, but legitimate macros, add-ins, automation, and administrative workflows can create the same parent-child relationship.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify selected Office parent processes starting selected interpreters while leaving unrelated parent processes, normal Office child processes, and incomplete events unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Determine whether the Office-to-interpreter chain was expected and inspect the document, command line, user, device, and adjacent process activity.
steps: Review the complete parent and child command lines, file paths, signer information, hashes, and process tree.
Identify the originating document, email, download, macro, add-in, or approved automation and confirm whether the user expected it.
Inspect adjacent file, network, registry, and process activity, then isolate the device and contain the account if execution is unexplained.
false_positives: Approved Office macros, add-ins, deployment tooling, troubleshooting scripts, and business automation

validation.expected_outcome: Match only when a selected Office parent starts a selected interpreter; do not match unrelated parents, benign Office children, or incomplete events.
